modern: None of these things ought to be called a man’s which do not belong to a man as a man. They are not required of a man, nor does man’s nature promise them, nor are they the means by which man’s nature reaches its end. So neither does the end of man lie in these things, nor yet what helps towards the accomplishment of this end; and what helps towards this end is what is good. Besides, if any of these things did belong to man, it would not be right for a man to despise them and set himself against them; nor would a man deserve praise who showed that he did not want these things, nor would he who denied himself any of them be good, if indeed these things were good. But as it is, the more of these things, or of other things like them, a man deprives himself of, or the more patiently he bears being deprived of any of them, the better a man he is, in just the same degree.
original: None of these things ought to be called a man’s, which do not belong to a man, as man. They are not required of a man, nor does man’s nature promise them, nor are they the means of man’s nature attaining its end. Neither then does the end of man lie in these things, nor yet that which aids to the accomplishment of this end, and that which aids toward this end is that which is good. Besides, if any of these things did belong to man, it would not be right for a man to despise them and to set himself against them; nor would a man be worthy of praise who snowed that he did not want these things, nor would he who stinted himself in any of them be good, if indeed these things were good. But now the more of these things a man deprives himself of, or of other things like them, or even when he is deprived of any of them, the more patiently he endures the loss, just in the same degree he is a better man.
